clue.text: It's got to change to accommodate language, primarily

definitions.text: It's got to change to accommodate language, primarily

indicators.note: the shuffled letters make room inside themselves for the next piece
the letters of the words before it are to be altered into a new order
primarily means taking only the first letter of the word language

explanation.surface: A grammar note: a word must alter its form to fit the language in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges IT'S GOT into GOTTIS around L, the first letter of 'language' signalled by 'primarily', which 'to accommodate' puts inside. Read whole, the clue describes the throat opening that shapes speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The vocal opening between the cords changes shape to produce speech sounds, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: The priest in Paris saves time for talk

indicators.note: saves means the priest word keeps the time letter within

parts.note: le curé is French for the parish priest

explanation.surface: A Paris priest makes time for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk given to an audience, as at a university.

clue.text: Send messages in tiny dry bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds in, so dry encloses tiny

parts.note: TT is teetotal, i.e. dry
wee means tiny

explanation.surface: Messages sent inside little empty bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' suggests message-in-a-bottle; it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To post short online messages, as on the social platform once called Twitter.

clue.text: This writer's former old thick coat

parts.note: the writer is I, so this writer's is I'm
past means former

explanation.surface: I am wearing my old heavy coat from former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick coat' sounds like clothing; it is paint laid on heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick layer of paint applied to a canvas so brushstrokes stand out.

clue.text: The Orient Express carried a lot of engineers

indicators.note: the fast word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: express as an adjective means fast
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of army engineers

explanation.surface: Evokes the Orient Express train ferrying a crowd of engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Orient Express' reads as the famous train, but the definition stops at 'The Orient'; 'Express' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is an old name for the countries of eastern Asia, the region also called by this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Last words of two people hugging one?

indicators.note: hugging means the two people phrase wraps round one

parts.note: à deux is French for for two people
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two lovers embrace a third as they say their final goodbyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewells, the French plural of goodbye, are what is said last.

clue.text: Articulate English sister spies tortoiseshell

parts.note: a nun is a sister
the CIA is the US spy agency
the shell of tortoise is its outer letters T and E

explanation.surface: An English nun tells of seeing a tortoiseshell cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortoiseshell' reads as a pattern or material; it is the shell, the outside letters, of 'tortoise'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce words clearly and distinctly, the verb sense of articulate.

clue.text: Support inserted in vessel or loudspeaker

parts.note: a stent is a tube inserted in a blood vessel to support it

explanation.surface: A medical note on a support placed in a blood vessel, or a loudspeaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion is part of what a stent is, not an instruction to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek herald in the Iliad with a huge voice, hence any very loud speaker.

clue.text: Eg articles a perfect shop's displayed

indicators.note: displayed means set out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Items for sale are on show in an ideal shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like goods in a shop; it is the grammar term for 'a' and 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles, like nouns and verbs, are grammatical word classes.

clue.text: Top expert brings in millions

indicators.note: the expert word takes the next letter inside itself

parts.note: an ace is an expert at something
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A top expert earns millions of pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean the highest point or peak of achievement.

clue.text: Cook stipulated chestnuts

indicators.note: to cook is to tamper with or rework, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: cook the chestnuts as stipulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnuts' looks like the food to be cooked; here it means stale old remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Old chestnuts are worn-out jokes or sayings, i.e. trite, overused remarks.

clue.text: They usually enclose 9 estimates

definitions.meaning: quotation marks usually surround reported speech, and 9 is parts of speech
a builder's estimates of price are also called by this word

explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is the answer at 9 down; the link is that reported speech sits inside quotation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas surround speech, and a tradesman's price estimates are also known as these.

clue.text: Cut short series about to be shown in gallery

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are displayed inside the gallery word

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
a run is a series, as of wins
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: An art series is curtailed just before it is exhibited in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous art gallery in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut short is to shorten by lopping off the end, the verb's exact sense.

clue.text: House officer working for Mark

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
COL is the abbreviation for colonel
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A house officer, a junior hospital doctor, is working for someone called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British house sharing one wall with its neighbour. 'House officer' looks like a hospital rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark, the dot over a comma, used between linked clauses.

clue.text: Did rail overrun, as some may say?

indicators.note: some speakers pronounce the overrun word nearly like the answer, so it is heard

parts.note: to overrun a country is to invade it

explanation.surface: Did a train overshoot the platform?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like the railway; it means to protest angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly; the past tense of speaking out strongly against something.

clue.text: Wander over island, one in NZ

indicators.note: over means the wandering word is turned backwards

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: A traveller roams across an island and ends up in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: An indigenous Polynesian person of New Zealand is one of this people.

clue.text: Crack small fruit I pinched

indicators.note: pinched means stolen, so the letter I is taken away from the fruit

parts.note: an olive is a fruit

explanation.surface: A confession: I stole a small piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to work it out.

clue.text: Bill deserts love for 2

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 2 down, clued as a talk

indicators.note: deserts means the bill leaves the love word

parts.note: adoration is deep love
an ad is a bill or advertising poster

explanation.surface: Bill walks out on his love.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech is a kind of talk delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Transport people back out of condition

indicators.note: the reversed word sits outside the condition word
back means the people word is read backwards

parts.note: a race is a people
state means condition

explanation.surface: Taking people back home when they are unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of condition' reads as unfit, but 'out of' means the reversed people word sits outside, with 'back' as its turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of car with extra load space at the back, a means of transport.

clue.text: He abandons ornamental hat and tackle

indicators.note: the letters of he leave the hat word

parts.note: a headdress is ornamental headwear

explanation.surface: A man discards a fancy hat and fishing tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackle' looks like gear; it is the verb, to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with a problem or task is to set about handling it.

clue.text: They qualify subtly and accurately, maybe

definitions.meaning: words that modify verbs, adjectives or other words
two examples of the word class ending in -ly

explanation.surface: Some candidates pass their exams finely and precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar words modifying verbs, of which subtly and accurately are examples.

clue.text: Polynesian bird once seen in clinic

indicators.note: the bird is placed within the clinic word

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium, a clinic
the moa was a flightless NZ bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: A Polynesian bird of the past is spotted in a clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Pacific islands of Samoa, which lie in Polynesia.

clue.text: Not a good time to limit latest banter

indicators.note: the outer words enclose the latest word, bounding it

parts.note: something not good is bad
an age is a period of time
in means fashionable, the latest thing

explanation.surface: It is not a good moment to restrict the newest teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-hearted teasing exchange of remarks; the French-derived word for playful talk.

clue.text: Musical director withdraws case

indicators.note: withdraws means the musical and director go backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A musical director pulls out of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical director' reads as one job; split it into EVITA and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical case, used for the indirect object in Latin and German.

clue.text: This puzzle has one note around the edge

indicators.note: the note goes round the edge word

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a hem is an edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A puzzle with a note written round its border.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's subject is parts of speech and speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A unifying subject running through a crossword's answers.

clue.text: Pat's blue uniform fitted in previously

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so politically right

indicators.note: the uniform letter is put inside the next word

parts.note: once means previously
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Pat is wearing a well-fitted blue uniform from before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a name; it is the adverb, as in 'answered pat'. Blue is the British Conservative party colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat as an adverb means at just the right moment, exactly when expected.

clue.text: Spanish runner featuring in outside broadcast

indicators.note: the letters appear within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Spanish athlete appears on a TV outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; in crosswords it is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A major river of north-east Spain; a river runs, hence runner.

clue.text: It soothes anyone at sea rounding Land's End

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the final letter
at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged
end means only the last letter of Land is used

explanation.surface: A sailor finds relief rounding Land's End, the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of England; here its 'End' is just the D of 'Land'.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller or soothing remedy; the noun sense of something that relieves.

clue.text: Criticise cast not taking sides, essentially

indicators.note: the word cast loses its outer letters

parts.note: per se means essentially, in itself

explanation.surface: Criticising an actor for being neutral, basically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking sides' looks like neutrality; it strips the ends from 'cast'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread damaging charges against someone, i.e. to slander or attack their reputation.
